text:
julie: Quick sync — quarterly least-privilege sweep is next week. I want to validate that admin-like roles (Admin*, Ops*, infra-owners) have expiry annotations or automated deprovisioning. Seen a spike in long-lived keys in KMS. Thoughts?

omar: We have two things to reconcile: 1) KMS key grants that list external principal ARNs, 2) IAM role bindings that are still attached to old oncall groups. For KMS, do we have a mapping from grant->assumer principal? If not, it's messy.

kevin: There's a grants export in S3: s3://audit-exports/kms/grants/2026-Q1/*.csv. It contains GrantId, GranteePrincipal, RetiringPrincipal, KeyId, CreateTime. The GranteePrincipal is often `arn:aws:iam::123:role/svc-data-processor`.

julie: Perfect. Can we join that to last seen API calls to decide active vs dormant grants? Example heuristic: any grantee with >1 Encrypt/Decrypt in the past 90 days = active.

leo: I'll throw together a Glue job to join S3 exports + CloudTrail. Mini SQL:

```
SELECT g.KeyId, g.GranteePrincipal, count(ct.eventName) as cnt
FROM kms_grants g
LEFT JOIN cloudtrail ct ON ct.userIdentity.arn = g.GranteePrincipal
WHERE ct.eventTime >= date_sub(current_date, 90)
GROUP BY g.KeyId, g.GranteePrincipal
HAVING cnt = 0
```

sara: Add a second join to IAM role tags to get owner info. If owner tag missing, fallback to git blame on infra repo. We should not auto-remove grants without manual review, but mark them in the cleanup queue.

omar: Side note: CloudTrail sometimes records `principalId` (AIDA...) instead of ARN for cross-account calls. We should normalize to ARN using STS AssumeRole events. There's a small mapping table `principal_id_to_arn` in our audit DB.

kevin: For entitlements we've been experimenting with TTL labels on roles. Terraform can set `lifecycle = { create_before_destroy = true }` but for TTLs we'd need a separate orchestration: set tag `access_expires=2026-04-10` and run a controller to revoke on expiry. Anyone comfortable with a short-lived controller?

julie: I think a Kubernetes CronJob in platform could run a reviewer bot that emails owners 7 days before expiry and auto-revokes if no response after 3 business days. Use the existing rotation key for KMS.

leo: On emails — ensure we include evidence (last 90 days of API ops) and a one-click remediation link that opens the remediation playbook in Console. Example payload: `mailto:owner@redwood.com?subject=Access%20expiry%20notice&body=See%20evidence%20%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fconsole.redwood.com%2Faccess%2Freview%2Ftoken123`

omar: Also important: exclude non-admin principals like Cognito users and federated product users. We should maintain an allowlist of principal patterns to ignore in admin sweep. Put it in `security-config/admin-sweep-ignore.yaml`.

kevin: For the least-privilege audit, we should snapshot all inline policies attached to admin groups and compute a delta vs a baseline 'restricted-admin' policy using policy language diff. Small script: `aws iam get-role-policy | jq -S . > /tmp/role.json` then use `policy-diff` tool (I'll add one).

julie: Great. If a role contains `KMS:*` or `iam:PassRole` we flag high priority.

sara: How do we handle cross-account KMS keys (partner integrations)? Some keys have ExternalAccounts in key policy. Those are allowed but need contractual owner. We need an attestation step: send to legal+contracts.

leo: I'll enrich the evidence bundle with key metadata: Alias, KeyRotationStatus, KeyPolicySummary. Use `aws kms describe-key --key-id` + `list-aliases --key-id`. Cache the results in Dynamo for 24h.

audit-bot: Export started: kms-grants-2026Q1.csv (rows: 8,412) :gear:

omar: On owner attribution heuristics: prefer explicit `owner` tag, then IAM role tag `maintainer`, then git blame on `infra/roles/*`, then as last resort label `owner:security-ops`. Keep a confidence score integer 0-100. Anything <70 goes to manual triage.

kevin: Agree. Let's standardize confidence buckets: 90-100 (auto safe), 70-89 (notify owner), <70 (block auto-remediate).

julie: Can we add an API endpoint for reviewers to claim an unknown item? e.g., POST /access-review/{id}/claim -> assigns to user and pauses auto-remediation.

sara: We'll need audit trail for claims. Use existing audit-log service and emit event `access_review.claimed` with metadata. Keep TTL for claims so it unclaims after 14 days.

leo: For the actual cleanup flow, propose: (1) mark stale grants in UI, (2) reviewers can 'revoke grant' which triggers a backend job that calls `RevokeGrant` and creates an issue in `#remediation` channel, (3) after revoke, run smoke tests for services using that key via our synthetic test harness.

omar: One gotcha: RevokeGrant is irreversible for some KMS keys if key material required. Must coordinate with product owners. Add a soft mode: `revoke_safety_check=false` to bypass only after explicit confirmation in Console.

kevin: Also ensure we include a rollback plan: `aws kms enable-key --key-id` and re-grant needed principals; store the previous grant ids in the evidence bundle.

julie: Action items: leo - add KMS metadata enrich + cache; kevin - policy diff tool + revoke soft-mode; omar - update ignore patterns list + principal normalization; sara - implement claim endpoint and audit events; julie - draft reviewer email template and runbook.

audit-bot: Export completed: 8412 grants, 152 admin-like roles touched, 2394 candidates marked for review :white_check_mark:

julie: Thanks all. Let's target a dry-run this week and full run next Tuesday. Keep changes small and tested. If you run into policy edge cases ping me.

kevin: I'll open PRs for the diff tool and the revoke controller today.

omar: I'll seed `security-config/admin-sweep-ignore.yaml` with current product principals.

leo: Will post the Glue job link and sample query in this thread when ready.

sara: I'll sketch claim API contract in OpenAPI and share a link.

julie: Good work. Closing loop here. :rocket:
